findings.title: The value of turning away changes with its object and stage
findings.claim: The focus wrongdoing lies in turning from the signs after receiving a reminder. Later, the closing command turns the same movement toward persistent refusers, while both sides wait.
findings.mechanism: The passive reminder is followed by thumma and the focus turn-away from the signs. In 32:30 the attributed turn-away is commanded toward the refusers and joined to reciprocal waiting. That contact locates the focus blame in abandoning the signs at renewed access, while the later command belongs to a different object and stage.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish the focus's blameworthy abandonment from every act of turning away, and can feel that settlement remains pending in the closing wait.
findings.containment: The focus charge remains intact; 32:30 does not make every withdrawal righteous. Its role may be a tactical command without an intended reversal of the focus wording. The target morphology for 32:30 is absent, so its word coordinates and role remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier is supplied directly, but the contextual root mapping and word indices are an unbound HFT attribution; the exact closing Arabic verifies surface contact only.

findings.title: Requital follows a live return window

findings.mechanism: The supplied 32:21 sequence places the nearer punishment before the greater one and gives return as its purpose. The focus predicate then carries registered censure and punitive-response facets; 32:29 states that faith at the day of victory will not benefit, and 32:30 leaves both sides waiting. Together they make the focus response the far edge of a warning-and-return sequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the threat as part of a sequence with an open return interval and a later limit, while censure and punishment remain two live aspects of the focus response.
findings.containment: The packet does not equate the nearer affliction with the focus requital or specify the timing between them. The HFT alternative that nearer discipline and final requital are distinct operations remains live; 32:29 and 32:30 add context without deciding that alternative.

findings.title: Signs appear in processes of provision and history
findings.claim: The focus signs can also be encountered in a material chain: water reaches barren ground, growth feeds animals and people, and the context asks whether they see. Nearby, the remains of destroyed generations are also presented as signs.
findings.mechanism: The focus sign-word and Lord-title meet the causal water-to-growth-to-consumption scene in 32:27 and its closing sight question. The supplied 32:26 connection gives a second context in which destroyed generations and their dwellings are presented as signs. Their contact makes reminder available in lived ecological provision and historical warning, while the focus turn-away can be read as refusal to recognize that dependence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the signs as more than verbal propositions: the world that sustains its observers and the remains of earlier communities can also confront them with visible evidence.
findings.containment: Revealed signs remain the focus wording's recoverable sense; ecological and historical processes add examples without replacing it. The 32:26 connection supplies exact Arabic but no target morphology, and the HFT's live alternative that the focus points primarily to revealed signs remains explicit.

epistemic.reason: The HFT context trace is legacy-unbound, while the 32:26 connection is a discovery nomination with exact Arabic but no morphology; both are used within those limits.

findings.mechanism: The focus signs meet the 32:24 sequence of patient, certain recipients who guide and lead. Its social relay supplies the independent trigger for the focus offender root's registered cutting facet: turning from signs can cut a possible route by which guidance reaches others.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees reception as capable of becoming guidance for others, so rejection can have a social consequence in addition to its personal one.
findings.containment: The focus Form IV active participle still names the criminal class; its cutting facet is an analogical root image, not a claim that the word literally means one who interrupts guidance. The HFT alternative that 32:24 is a specific historical example rather than a general consequence remains live.

findings.title: Cutting and barrenness as an image of severance
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the offender's root-level cutting image meets barren ground and regrowth, allowing the focus turn from signs to appear as self-severance from a cultivating process.
findings.mechanism: The focus offender-class carrier has a registered cutting branch. In 32:27 the attributed barren-ground and regrowth coordinates form a before-and-after material image; the focus Lord-title's cultivation facet connects that growth back to the sign relation. Their contact turns the outlier into an ecological image of attention severed from nurture.
findings.reader_payoff: The offender label can hold a material image of cutting oneself off from what is being cultivated, rather than remaining only a legal category.
findings.containment: The ordinary criminal-class sense stays intact. Cutting is a root-level analogy, not an etymology or a claim that the Form IV active participle literally means cutter. The barren-ground mapping and context roles remain HFT-attributed.

epistemic.reason: The packet marks this as exploratory and explicitly bounds it as a cross-root material analogy; the relevant context root mappings remain legacy-unbound.
